web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Life of Pi by Yann Martel
web_evidence.note: A sustained Chapter 1 excerpt, published with the copyright holder's permission, has Pi narrating his life and studies throughout as 'I' and 'my'.

web_evidence.title: First-person Narration in Life of Pi
web_evidence.note: This scholarly structural analysis identifies homodiegetic first-person narration at both levels: Pi narrates the embedded shipwreck story, while a first-person mask narrator supplies the frame and verification.

web_evidence.title: Life of Pi
web_evidence.note: The literary reference entry states that Pi is the first-person narrator of much of the novel and describes the work as combining first-person accounts by Pi and the Author with local interview transcripts.

person_note: The event quotes repeatedly expose Pi as a participating 'I' recounting his childhood, religion, shipwreck, and survival. The authorized opening excerpt independently confirms that voice, while scholarly whole-book analysis resolves the frame: the occasional Author/mask narrator is also first person, so the presence of two narrators does not make the novel ALTERNATING under this methodology. Dialogue and interview-transcript excerpts are local speech, and generic 'you' in maxims is not second-person narration. No credible contrary person evidence remains.
